behavior.description: Mutually exclusive Crohn's disease Paris behavior. B1: nonstricturing, nonpenetrating; B2: stricturing, including fixed narrowing, stenosis, or obstruction attributed to Crohn's disease; B3: penetrating, including intra-abdominal fistula, sinus tract, inflammatory mass, phlegmon, abscess, or perforation attributed to Crohn's disease. Do not use B3 for isolated perianal disease alone; B2B3: both stricturing and penetrating Crohn's disease are documented, either at the same time or at different times; UNKNOWN: Crohn's disease is documented, but behavior is unknown or unclear; NONE_OF_THE_ABOVE: None of the above, such as not mentioned, patient does not have Crohn's disease.

CDParisLocationL4aMention.description:
Crohn's disease Paris L4a modifier.

Use when Crohn's disease involves the upper GI tract *PROXIMAL* to the
Ligament of Treitz, such as esophageal, gastric, or duodenal Crohn's disease.

Do not use PRESENT for nonspecific gastritis, reflux, vomiting, abdominal pain, or
unrelated upper-GI symptoms unless attributed to Crohn's disease.

Prefer explicit Paris codes when present.
Do not extract family history of IBD, negated IBD, rule-out IBD, or suspected/probable/working-diagnosis IBD.

l4a.description: Crohn's disease Paris L4a modifier. PRESENT: documented Crohn's involvement proximal to the Ligament of Treitz. ABSENT: documented Crohn's disease and L4a/proximal upper-GI involvement is explicitly absent, ruled out, or described as not involved. UNKNOWN: Crohn's disease is documented and upper-GI involvement is mentioned, but the location is unclear or cannot be assigned to L4a versus L4b. NOT_MENTIONED: L4a is not addressed, or the patient does not have Crohn's disease.

CDParisLocationL4bMention.description:
Crohn's disease Paris L4b modifier.

Use when Crohn's disease involves the upper small bowel *DISTAL* to the
Ligament of Treitz and proximal to the distal 1/3 ileum, such as jejunal
or proximal ileal Crohn's disease.

Do not use PRESENT for nonspecific abdominal pain, nonspecific enteritis,
nonspecific small-bowel inflammation, or unrelated GI symptoms unless
attributed to Crohn's disease.

Prefer explicit Paris codes when present.
Do not extract family history of IBD, negated IBD, rule-out IBD, or suspected/probable/working-diagnosis IBD.

description:
An object-model for annotations of inflammatory bowel disorder observations
found in a patient's chart, related to Paris classification.
Take care to avoid false positives, like confusing information that only
appears in family history for patient history. Annotations should indicate
the relevant details of the finding, as well as some additional evidence
metadata to validate findings post-hoc.
